chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three groups intercede with God, the Mighty and Exalted, and their intercession is accepted: the Prophets, then the Scholars, then the Martyrs.'

key_terms.إِلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: With God, the Mighty and Exalted

ai.seo_question: Who are the three groups that intercede with God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* establishes a hierarchical structure of intercession (*shafa'ah*), placing the Prophets at the apex, followed by the Scholars (*Ulama*) as the inheritors of prophetic knowledge, and finally the Martyrs (*Shuhada*). In Shia tradition, the inclusion of Scholars highlights their unique spiritual authority and role as guides, distinguishing them as a distinct class of intercessors alongside the Prophets and Martyrs. This triad underscores the continuity of divine guidance from revelation to scholarly interpretation and ultimate sacrifice.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-197 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry, on the authority of Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus’adat ibn Sadaqah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB)

that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “There are three groups who intercede on behalf of someone with the Honorable the Exalted God and their intercession will be accepted: the Prophets, then the scholars; and then the martyrs.”
